summary: Edo Shonin works in religious and Buddhist studies, having earned a PhD at Nottingham Trent University. Attested in 2015, Shonin served as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre.

Edoardo Siani is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned an M.A. in Social Anthropology from SOAS (2014–2018). He held posts at SOAS (2018–2019), Kyoto University (2018–2020), and Ca' Foscari University of Venice (2020).

Edouard Müller-Hess (1853–1923) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin, Tübingen, and Leipzig (Ph.D.). He succeeded Siegfried Goldschmidt (1877–1880), taught German at Cardiff (1883–1888), and was Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Bern (1888).

Eduard Buschmann (1805–1880) was a linguist who studied at Göttingen, Berlin under Franz Bopp, and Königsberg (Hon. Ph.D.). He held posts at the Royal Library of Berlin (1832), the Prussian Academy of Sciences (1851), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1840–1880).

Eduard Böhmer (1827–1906) was a linguist who studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1847–1851). He later held academic appointments at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1859–1872) and the University of Strasbourg (~1872–1879).

Eduard Erkes (1891–1958) was a sinologist who studied under August Conrady at the University of Leipzig (~1910–1913). He succeeded Conrady, held a post at Leipzig (~1917–1958), and also held a position at Humboldt University of Berlin.

Eduard Hermann (1869–1950) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Freiburg, Leipzig, and Jena under Berthold Delbrück. He held posts at Kiel (1913), Frankfurt (1914), and Göttingen (1917–1937), succeeding Jacob Wackernagel in 1917.

Eduard Müller (1854–1908) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied under Ernst Kuhn and completed his Inauguraldissertation at the University of Leipzig (~1873–1874), later serving as professor at the University of Bern (~1886–1908).

Eduard Prokosch (1876–1938) was a linguist educated at Charles University, Vienna, the National German-American Teachers' Seminary, Chicago, and Leipzig (Ph.D.). He held positions at Wisconsin-Madison (1905–1913), Texas at Austin (1913–1919), Bryn Mawr (1919–1928), and Yale (1929).

Eduard Röer (1805–1866) specialized in Indology and philosophy, studying at Jena, Königsberg under J. F. Herbart, and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He held posts at Berlin (1833–1838), the East India Company (~1839–1861), and The Asiatic Society (~1841–1861).

Eduard Sachau (1845–1930) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics who earned his Ph.D. at Halle-Wittenberg (~1867). He held posts at Vienna, Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1876), and the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1887).

Eduard Schwyzer (1874–1943) was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Zurich under Adolf Kaegi and studied at Leipzig. He held professorships at the University of Zurich (from 1909), Bonn (1927), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1932–1939).

Eduard Sievers (1850–1932) was a linguist who earned his doctorate at Leipzig under Friedrich Zarncke. He held professorships at the University of Jena (1871–1883), University of Tübingen (1883–1887), Halle-Wittenberg (1887–1892), and University of Leipzig (1892–1922).

Eduard Thommen (1880–1961) was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Basel (~1898–1901), the University of Paris, the University of Oxford, and the University of Göttingen (~1901–1903), where he completed his PhD under Jacob Wackernagel.

Eduard Wölfflin (1831–1908) was a linguist who studied at the University of Basel (~1849–1851) and the University of Göttingen (~1851–1854). He held posts at the University of Zurich (~1861–1869), Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1869–1880), and Munich (~1880–1905).

Eduard Zeller (1814–1908) studied at Tübingen and worked in philosophy and religious studies. He held posts at Tübingen (~1840–1847), Bern (~1847–1849), Marburg (~1849–1862), Heidelberg (~1862–1872), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1872–1894).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under the supervision of Yakupitiyage Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.

Eduardo Luigi De Stefani (1869–1921) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied under Paolo Emilio Pavolini. In 1910, he held a post teaching Latin and Greek grammar at Sapienza University of Rome.

Edvard Brandes (1847–1931) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Niels Ludvig Westergaard, earning an M.A. in Oriental Philology (~1865–1872) and a Ph.D. (~1872–1879).

Edvard Westermarck (1862–1939) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at the University of Helsinki (~1881–1889). He later held academic posts at the London School of Economics (~1904–1929) and Åbo Akademi University (~1918–1932).
